source.title: The Geometric Structure of Models Learning Sparse Data
source.authors: Thomas Walker; T. Roddenberry; Ahmed Imtiaz Humayun; Randall Balestriero; R. Baraniuk

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures grokking-related accuracy and centroid alignment, and tests how training interventions change the epochs needed to reach a grokked-state criterion. It is not an explicit replication of the original study's full method and measure.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports the grokked-state attainment rate, epochs, speed-up and paired-test p-value for each training method and task; these are recorded below. Figure 2 reports training/test accuracy and centroid alignment over training, but its plotted values are not stated numerically. The paper's table and text about tabular RFAM robustness, normal alignment on other datasets, and cited findings do not report additional results on the claim versions and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses standard grokking setups (XOR, sparse parity, MNIST, modular addition) as a testbed for its own regularizer, GrokAlign. Table 1 reports only epochs to reach a test-accuracy threshold for its method against Grokfast, OrthoGrad and a baseline. No row records training-accuracy saturation timing, a chance-to-near-perfect jump, or a training-set-size sweep, so the delay itself is never quantified. The only train/test trajectory (Figure 2, Nanda et al. pipeline) is plotted without stated values. The centroid-alignment measure is the study's own geometric construct, not a progress measure of the generalizing circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that normal alignment is a structural signature of models trained in sparse settings, and that GrokAlign accelerates grokking across tasks with the largest, most consistent speed-ups, while Grokfast and OrthoGrad vary. They also prove that normal-aligned classifiers optimize norm-constrained training and are maximally locally robust. They attribute grokking to delayed feature learning (lazy-to-rich), citing prior work rather than testing it.
record.recipe_differences: The grokking experiments use the authors' stated XOR, sparse-parity, MNIST and modular-addition setups and compare GrokAlign, Grokfast and OrthoGrad by epochs to task-specific grokked-state criteria. This is not presented as an explicit replication of the original grokking recipe; the Figure 2 transformer pipeline is stated to be identical to Nanda et al. (2022).
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking attainment and epochs vary by task, loss and training intervention. GrokAlign reaches the criterion in all five Table 1 setups; OrthoGrad reaches it in only 20% of XOR runs and none of the MNIST squared-error or modular-addition runs. Grokfast results also vary by setup.

fits_no_version.finding: A one-layer transformer on modular arithmetic becomes centroid-aligned during training, and centroid alignment correlates with train-to-test generalization (Figure 2, figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A Jacobian/power-diagram geometric measure (centroid alignment) tracks generalization during grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: A Jacobian-norm regularizer (GrokAlign) cuts epochs to the grokked state by 1.5x to 19.8x across five setups; Grokfast and OrthoGrad give variable or no speed-up.

record.problems: Table 1 reports aggregate results over ten random initializations and a grokked-state threshold, rather than full training- and test-accuracy trajectories. It does not compare training-set sizes. Figure 2 values are only plotted, without numerical values in the text. The paper's tested settings do not establish the specific Fourier-algorithm or memorization-removal account.

untested.parts: Delay between train saturation and test jump, chance-level start, and the delay growing as the training set shrinks; none are quantified.
Fourier/generalizing circuit formation, memorization removal, and progress measures anticipating the jump.
Delay on non-algorithmic data with stated train/test timing; switching via initialization scale or weight norm.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4: Table 1 measures only epochs to a test-accuracy threshold under competing acceleration methods. Most rows are method comparisons and are relinked to none. The reader's labels were dropped because no row quantifies the grokking delay. The Figure 2 pipeline replicates Nanda et al., an original source, and reports no values.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report the full training-accuracy and test-accuracy trajectories for the Table 1 setups, chance-level starting accuracy, or a sweep showing that the delay grows as training data shrinks. Figure 2 plots train/test accuracy for modular addition but does not state their numerical trajectories in the text.

The paper measures centroid alignment over training on modular addition and reports its correlation with generalization. It does not identify a Fourier algorithm, measure removal of memorizing components, or establish that a continuous measure anticipates the accuracy jump.

The paper includes non-algorithmic XOR and MNIST tasks, but does not sweep initialization scale or weight norm to switch grokking delays on or off, and does not test text or molecule data. GrokAlign is a Jacobian regularizer, not an initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
The paper does not test whether low norm selects a more efficient generalizing circuit, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
The paper does not compare the learned algorithms across runs.
The paper does not test whether grokking delays are artifacts of adaptive optimizers or floating-point/softmax limits.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Baseline pipelines for XOR, sparse parity, MNIST with both losses, and modular addition
reader_labels.reason: Each baseline reports 100% reaching its stated test-accuracy-based grokked-state criterion, at the listed epochs (R01, R05, R09, R13, R17). This supports grokking-state attainment in these setups, but not the full train/test trajectory or training-set-size relation.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: One-layer transformer trained on modular arithmetic, as plotted in Figure 2
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports train/test accuracy plotted alongside centroid alignment, but the numerical trajectory and timing are not stated; the row is therefore only partial evidence for the accuracy-trajectory component (R21, R22).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The baseline XOR and MNIST setups reach their reported grokked-state criteria, providing results on non-algorithmic tasks (R01, R09, R13).
